svg.style: background: #090d16; border-radius: 12px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
svg.text: The 4 Critical Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Systems
Why Naive Autonomous Agent Swarms Stall, Infinite Loop, or Hallucinate in Production

g.text: 1. Circular Ping-Pong Deadlock
Agent A asks Agent B for data; Agent B requests clarification from Agent A.
Agent A: "Clarify table schema"
Agent B: "Provide query first"
Symptom: 85 API calls in 90 seconds until rate limit exhaustion ($40 burned).
2. The "Telephone Game" Context Drift
Critical constraints are summarized away through successive agent handoffs.
User: "Draft refund policy for EU residents under 14-day statutory law."
→ Summary A: "Draft refund policy" → Agent C writes US 30-day warranty!
Symptom: Compliance violation due to semantic loss across handoffs.
3. Split-Brain State Desynchronization
Two agents execute concurrent tool calls without transactional locking.
Agent 1: Updates DB record
status = "PROCESSING"
Agent 2: Reads stale cache
status = "PENDING"
Symptom: Double charges, corrupted states, duplicate emails dispatched.
4. Cascading Tool Stampede
An agent spawns 50 parallel research subagents that DDoS internal APIs.
Supervisor spawns: Subagent[1..50] each querying internal Elasticsearch
→ Connection pool exhausted → Database connection timeout (503 Service Unavailable)
Symptom: Production infrastructure outage triggered by unthrottled agent concurrency.
